clue.text: King Edward possibly seemed upset to take over?

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, so in a down clue the run of letters reads bottom to top
to take from a phrase is to lift a run of letters straight out of it

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A historical King Edward looked distressed at having to seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' does double duty as part of the run of letters and as the signal to read it backwards. King Edward is a popular British potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A spud is slang for a potato, and King Edward is one well-known variety, so it is a definition by example.

clue.text: Cycling, travel north or finally leave state?

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, so the built string is rotated to start elsewhere

parts.note: to go is to travel
N is the compass abbreviation for north
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the last letter of leave

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up a trip: head north on a bike, or simply quit the state?
explanation.walkthrough: GO, N, OR and E join to GONORE; moving GON from the front to the back gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty United States, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Yates pub struggling over time in scenic location

indicators.note: a struggling pub is in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Yates bar, a British pub chain, has been doing badly for a while despite its pretty setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a place admired for its scenery, a synonym for a picturesque location.

clue.text: Racehorse English mind Conservative withdrawing from Cesarewitch surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the leftover letters come out in a new order
things withdrawing from a word leave it, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the name of the horse race, taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
wit is intelligence, the mind
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A racing note: an English horse beat the Tory favourite in the Cesarewitch, a big flat race at Newmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E, WIT and C from CESAREWITCH leaves SAREC H, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a steeplechaser, a horse trained to race over fences.

clue.text: Delay ringing new firm to install small panelling

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so this word wraps around what follows
to install something is to put it inside, so the small letter sits within

parts.note: to wait is to delay
N is the abbreviation for new
S is the abbreviation for small
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business is held up while a new contractor fits some small wooden panels.
explanation.walkthrough: Two container signals work together: the delay rings everything, and the small letter is installed between new and firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden lining on the lower part of a room's walls, so it is a kind of panelling.

clue.text: Dropping soft drink causes stain

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Spilling a fizzy drink leaves a mark on your clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drink' reads as one thing, a fizzy pop, but soft is the letter to drop from the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is a stain on someone's reputation, an insinuation that blemishes their character.

clue.text: Individual briefly working with leading DUP politician perhaps

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a unit is a single individual thing
on means working, as in switched on
leading means first, written 1ST with the 1 as letter I

explanation.surface: A lone figure briefly collaborating with a top Northern Irish party member.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland. Crosswords often read the numeral 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A DUP member supports keeping Northern Ireland in the United Kingdom, which makes them an example of a unionist.

clue.text: Contemporary gift given to daughter away on vacation

parts.note: a present is a gift
D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of away

explanation.surface: A modern present handed to a daughter who is off on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Present-day as an adjective means belonging to now, a synonym for contemporary.

clue.text: Son splits modest prize money

indicators.note: something that splits a word goes into the middle of it

parts.note: pure in the sense of chaste, modest
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son takes his share of a small prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is the sum of money offered as a prize, especially in boxing or racing.

clue.text: Star performer, that woman overshadowing band on bill

indicators.note: to overshadow is to cast a cover over, so this word envelops the rest

parts.note: her refers to that woman

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another is written after it

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement
a band is a stripe or line

explanation.surface: The star upstaging the rest of the group on a concert poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a musical group in a story about star performers; here it is a stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the main act whose name appears at the top of a bill, the star of the show.

clue.text: Bet United boss backtracks about places for substitutes?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the rest
to backtrack is to go back the way you came, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a boss is a raised stud or knob
a go is an attempt or turn, a bet in the sense of a try
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football manager at United reverses his position on a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United boss' looks like a football manager, but boss is a knob. The question mark flags that dugouts are only one kind of place where substitutes sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dugouts are the sheltered benches beside a pitch where managers and reserve players wait.

clue.text: Channel dominated essentially by darts

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or heart of the word, its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of dominated
arrows is the slang name for darts

explanation.surface: A TV channel whose schedule is mostly darts coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television alongside darts; here it is a stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrows are a narrow stretch of water linking two larger bodies, so a channel.

clue.text: Club runs out of alcoholic spirit

indicators.note: something out of a word has left it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: brandy is a distilled spirit
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A social club has run dry of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' reads as a members' bar; here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandy is a curved stick used in the old game of the same name, an early form of hockey club.

clue.text: House with superior Spring borders

indicators.note: in a down clue superior means placed higher, so this piece is written above the other

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap
Aries is the first house of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A grand house with a lovely spring garden edged with flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is an astrological house, and in a down answer the superior piece is written first.
explanation.definitionFit: Boundaries are the lines marking the edges of an area, its borders.

clue.text: Social class when very young

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a party or gathering, as a noun
second meaning: the first school year in England, for four and five-year-olds

explanation.surface: Remembering being in a particular social class as a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social class' reads as one phrase about rank, but the split falls between the two words. In England children start school in the Reception year.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal party, a social, and Reception is also the infants' first class at primary school.

clue.text: One of many taken by tourer around capital?

definitions.text: One of many taken by tourer around capital?

parts.words: One of many taken by tourer
parts.note: surface reading: a holiday snap, one of many photos a tourist takes
setter's reading: one of the many Underground lines a visitor rides round London

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests photographs; the thing taken is a Tube line, as on the London Underground the visitor takes one of several named lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piccadilly line is one of the London Underground routes, much used by tourists as it serves Heathrow and the West End.

clue.text: Simple chap isn't used to travelling round Italy

indicators.note: travelling round means moving about, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these four words
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A naive man who has never been abroad before tours Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated means lacking worldly experience or refinement, a synonym of simple in the sense of naive.

clue.text: Vendor, more flexible accommodating one

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room inside, so this word holds the other

parts.note: suppler is the comparative of supple
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seller who is more willing than most to bend and meet a customer's needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier is a firm or person who provides goods for sale, a vendor.

clue.text: Repeatedly half-cut, begins to ogle aunt; that's rude

indicators.note: each of the following words is cut in half in turn, with only its back half kept

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk man keeps leering at his aunt, which is impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which hides the instruction to halve each word. Keep the second half of each: INS, O, LE, NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means disrespectful and impertinent, close in sense to rude.

clue.text: Filled in document to maintain exercise in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word is written in reverse
to maintain is to hold, so this word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a sit-up is an abdominal exercise

explanation.surface: A retiree has filed paperwork promising to keep up gym routines.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a stand-in, so someone who deputised filled in for another.

clue.text: Hole on golf course Harry set up

parts.note: to dog someone is to harry or pursue them

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to gel is to set, like a jelly

explanation.surface: A golfer named Harry has laid out one of the holes on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name but is the verb to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a golf hole whose fairway bends sharply partway along, like a dog's hind leg.

clue.text: Inability to control movement of an articulated vehicle

parts.note: an is the same article as a, used before a vowel

indicators.note: articulated means pronounced clearly, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: a taxi is a vehicle for hire

explanation.surface: An articulated lorry that the driver cannot steer properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated vehicle' reads as a lorry with a hinged trailer, but articulated is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxy, also ataxia, is the medical term for loss of coordination of bodily movements.

clue.text: Form of discrimination is depressing male after time

indicators.note: in a down clue depressing means pressing down on top, so this piece sits above
after means coming later, so this pair follows the other piece

parts.note: an age is a period of time
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man who finds an unfair kind of prejudice depressing, as he gets older.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against people because of how old they are, one form of discrimination.

clue.text: Give new name to flipping large European farm machinery

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large
E is the abbreviation for European
a baler is a farm machine that makes bales of hay

explanation.surface: A farmer wants to rename some big, dratted European tractor equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse word on the machinery; it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To relabel is to put a fresh label on something, giving it a new name.

clue.text: Bunny having more than one disease

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cartoon rabbit ... Bunny
second meaning: plural of the informal word for an infection

explanation.surface: A pet rabbit suffering from several illnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a forename: Bugs is the first name of the Warner Bros rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is the cartoon rabbit's name, and bugs are also minor infections or illnesses in everyday speech.

clue.text: Sanguine about unspecified number wanting old coins

indicators.note: about can mean moved around, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
wanting means lacking, so that letter is missing

parts.note: taken as written
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An optimist unconcerned about a few missing antique coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Guineas were British gold coins worth 21 shillings, last minted in 1814.

clue.text: Exeter, say, attracting back from Bedford, top-ranked player

parts.note: Exeter is the seat of a bishop, a see

indicators.note: back from points to the rear end of the word, its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of Bedford

explanation.surface: A tennis star from Exeter draws support from Bedford, two English towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exeter, say' looks like a sports team or a town, but it is a cathedral city with its own bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed is a player ranked in a tournament draw so the best do not meet early on.

clue.text: Coming out of crisis, changing philosophy ultimately to energy

indicators.note: changing one thing to another swaps a letter for a new one

parts.note: an emergency is a crisis

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of philosophy
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Emerging from a crisis by switching to an energetic approach.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the final Y of EMERGENCY with E.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergence is the act of coming out into view, so the two are noun synonyms.

clue.text: Man, say, behind source of ludicrous yarn

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this piece follows the other
the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of ludicrous
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man is responsible for spinning a ridiculous tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tall story; it is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread, a kind of yarn used for stockings.
